This borders on lunacy." Can you -- can you even suppose which 80.000 automatic weapons he is referring to?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV VUKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think he's referring to the illegally distributed weapons, the illegally imported weapons?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV VUKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the atmosphere among the Serbian people after this programme was broadcast, after they saw how these weapons were being imported illegally and how they intended to use them?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV VUKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terrible fear reigned among the Serbs after that programme. They started saying, "We want weapons too." They asked me to get them weapons. That's why I went to see Kir, and I asked him to go and explain to the Serbs how they can get hold of weapons. Only in that way and in no other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How would it have been received if any of the current Serbian leaders had come out before the people and said, "Let them have their 80.000 weapons. Don't do anything. Just keep quiet."

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV VUKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, they would have booed him off the stage and later they would probably stone him. The reaction would have been very serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you one more thing regarding the Prosecution's last question. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is all, Mr. Vukcevic. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV VUKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, the document on the screen, was that the one we discussed in private session during your cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, no. This is a transcript of a video we showed earlier during my cross-examination and does not need to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's not about the document on the screen. It's about the document that we just -- Mr. Zivanovic just discussed with the witness, and there is perhaps a problem with confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. For the sake of -- well, just to be on the safe side, perhaps it's better to redact the portion which begins at page 94, line 5, and this is the question and answer relating to 65 ter 6588, all the way to page 94, line 25. It doesn't reveal the originator or anything, but if you want to be on the safe side, it doesn't hurt to redact it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So out of an abundance of caution, Mr. Zivanovic, do you agree that we redact that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be redacted. Mr. Vukcevic, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back home. The court usher will escort you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to thank you for your understanding and for everything that has been offered to me here, particularly the chance to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We thank the interpreters and the supporting staff for making this extra hearing possible. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of September, 2014, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.56 p.m.,
